name: CapCut Overlay Path Keyframes
use_when: A sticker, arrow, photo, text layer, PNG, or video overlay needs to enter, point, travel, or exit on a custom path.
A travel map, product callout, tutorial pointer, or social graphic needs a simple animated path inside CapCut.
A default slide animation cannot hit the exact target, route, or timing.
Multiple photos or proof images need simple slide-in/out motion beside a talking-head speaker.
A sticker or object should follow a gaze, finger point, route, or offscreen exit with manual control.
avoid_when: The overlay would cover the subject, captions, product, UI, proof, or map label it is supposed to clarify.
A built-in animation gives the same result with less keyframe risk.
The overlay has no focus, proof, callout, or transition job.
The speaker was filmed centered and there is no safe negative space for the overlay.

timeline_pattern.slide_rule: Start the overlay outside the visible frame when it should slide on, then hold on the target before sliding out.
timeline_pattern.route_rule: For a travel or map path, set origin and destination keyframes and keep the moving object small enough not to hide labels.
timeline_pattern.callout_rule: For arrows and stickers, the final position should point to a real detail before it exits.
timeline_pattern.object_path_rule: For a sticker or object path, set the object size/flip/rotation first, then keyframe position from the starting point to the intended destination or offscreen exit.
timeline_pattern.custom_vs_preset_rule: Use manual keyframes when the overlay needs a custom path; use animation presets for ordinary slide-ins.
timeline_pattern.photo_stack_rule: For supporting photos, frame the speaker to one side, resize images into negative space, stagger entries, and add matching out animations.

motion.rule: Animate position first, then scale or rotation only if it clarifies the path or callout.

keyframe_values.entry_hold: Hold the overlay after it reaches the target until the viewer can understand the callout.
keyframe_values.path_spacing: Use wider spacing for travel-map drift and closer spacing for quick social sticker entrances.
keyframe_values.offscreen_exit: Move the final keyframe fully offscreen when the object is meant to leave the scene rather than remain as a callout.
keyframe_values.exit: Move the overlay fully offscreen or fade it before the next visual focus competes.
keyframe_values.photo_slide: A calm professional slide can last around 1.0-1.4 seconds when the image remains readable.

sound.rule: Use a small pop or whoosh only when the overlay entrance, route start, or exit needs emphasis; keep speech dominant.

captions.rule: Keep overlay paths out of caption safe areas unless the overlay is replacing the caption text.

color.rule: Overlay color should contrast with the background without hiding map labels or product detail.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use overlay x/y expressions with timed start/end positions; add alpha fades for exits and render contact sheets for collisions.
implementation.remotion: Represent overlayPath with assetId, startFrame, endFrame, x/y keyframes, optional scale/rotation, holdFrames, and safeRegions.
implementation.blender: Animate a plane or object along a 2D/3D path with camera-safe framing.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Add the sticker/photo/text/video overlay, set size/flip/rotation before path keyframes, create a starting keyframe or use a simple in animation, move it offscreen or to origin, add destination and exit keyframes when custom timing is needed, and preview the full path at phone size.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use Essential Graphics or imported PNG/video layers with Position/Scale/Rotation keyframes and Ease In/Out; nest if several overlays travel together.

common_mistakes: Letting the overlay path cover the exact detail it should point at.
Using default slide direction when a custom route or target is needed.
Forgetting to add a hold after the overlay reaches the focus point.
Leaving the overlay onscreen after its spoken concept has passed.
Using a built-in animation when the sticker should follow a precise gaze, finger, route, or exit path.
Using unlicensed map, sticker, icon, photo, or stock assets in a publishable project.
qc: Does the overlay enter from the intended start point and land on the intended focus?
Does it hold long enough to understand the callout or route?
Does the path avoid faces, captions, UI, products, proof, and map labels?
Does the overlay exit or clear before the next focus beat?
Are external assets source/license-ready for real projects?
If this is a photo stack, was the speaker framed with enough negative space?
